title: Free operadic extensions in cocomplete coefficients and their coefficient-change mate
statement:
Use the universe and monoidal infinity-category conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads and inert-preserving algebras of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability], using only its definitions. Let $u:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ be a map of small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads such that $\mathcal M_{[0]}$ and $\mathcal N_{[0]}$ are Kan complexes and $u_{[0]}$ is an equivalence. Let $\mathcal V$ be a cocomplete monoidal infinity category whose tensor preserves small colimits separately. Restriction $u^*:\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal N}(\mathcal V)\to\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal V)$ admits a left adjoint $u_!^{\mathcal V}$. Its unit $\eta_B:B\to u^*u_!^{\mathcal V}B$ induces natural equivalences $\operatorname{Map}(u_!^{\mathcal V}B,C)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(B,u^*C)$ by precomposition with $\eta_B$. Suppose $\mathcal W$ has the same cocompleteness and tensor properties and $F:\mathcal V\to\mathcal W$ is strong monoidal and preserves small colimits. Write $F_{*,\mathcal M}$ and $F_{*,\mathcal N}$ for postcomposition on the respective algebra categories. The canonical mate
$$u_!^{\mathcal W}F_{*,\mathcal M}\longrightarrow F_{*,\mathcal N}u_!^{\mathcal V}$$
is an equivalence of functors. Its component at $B$ is adjunct to
$$F_{*,\mathcal M}B\xrightarrow{F_{*,\mathcal M}\eta_B}F_{*,\mathcal M}u^*u_!^{\mathcal V}B\simeq u^*F_{*,\mathcal N}u_!^{\mathcal V}B.$$
These are natural transformations of infinity-category functors; in particular the equivalence includes all higher homotopies and the displayed compatibility with the adjunction unit. No presentability assumption is made.

source.place: Gepner-Haugseng, Enriched infinity-categories via nonsymmetric infinity-operads, v4 (2019). Theorem A.4.6 (existence), Proposition A.4.3 (unit mapping-space adjunction), and Lemma A.4.7 (the specified natural mate). Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Fix an $\mathcal M$-algebra $B$. For every colour $n\in\mathcal N_{[1]}$, use the active slice $K_n$ and diagram $T_n$ of [lem-coef-operadic-free-cocone-criterion]. They are small: slices and homotopy pullbacks of the given small operads remain in the smaller universe. The unique active arrows from each $[r]$ to $[1]$ form a coherent base transformation from the base of $T_n$ to the constant $[1]$-diagram. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] to the monoidal cocartesian fibration of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]. This gives a coherent cocartesian transformation $T_n\to D_n$ with $D_n:K_n\to\mathcal V$. At $(m,\alpha)$, if $m$ lies over $[r]$, its value is $B(m_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes B(m_r)$; at $r=0$ it is the tensor unit. The arrows and higher simplices of $D_n$ are given by this coherent transport, rather than by choosing unrelated tensors at vertices.

source.place: Definitions A.4.1 and A.2.1; cocartesian push to the unary fibre in Proposition A.2.10 Read online; agent reconstruction, archive WANTED.

proof.text: We record the elementary unary criterion needed below, using the operadic-cocone definition of [def-coef-operadic-correspondence]. Let $T:K\to\mathcal V^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$ have unary cocartesian push $D$, and let $T\to v$ be an active cocone with unary push $D\to v$. By the precomposition equivalence of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport], active cocones $T\to w$ are equivalent to transformations $D\to\operatorname{const}_K(w)$, and active arrows from the unary apex to $w$ are $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(v,w)$. For a fixed tuple $L$, put $\ell=\bigotimes L$, with $\ell=\mathbf1$ for the empty tuple. The same precomposition equivalence applied to the diagram $L\oplus T$ identifies its active cocones with transformations $\ell\otimes D\to\operatorname{const}_K(w)$; applied to $T\oplus L$ it gives transformations $D\otimes\ell\to\operatorname{const}_K(w)$. These identifications follow from the cocartesian tensor transports and their composition in [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], and they intertwine restriction along the cocone. Consequently, if $D\to v$ is colimiting and tensoring separately preserves its colimit, the dual mapping-space cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes both context restriction maps equivalences. Conversely, take the empty context to deduce that $D\to v$ is colimiting by that same criterion. Thus the active cocone is operadically colimiting exactly when its unary push is colimiting, under the stated tensor preservation. This is the mapping-space calculation of Gepner--Haugseng Proposition A.2.10, written here rather than made a new node.

source.place: Definition A.2.1, Corollary A.2.7 and Proposition A.2.10; elementary deduction from the cited transport and cocone statements, agent reconstruction, archive WANTED.

proof.text: Let $\bar D_n$ be a colimiting cocone on $D_n$ with apex $c_n$, which exists by cocompleteness since $K_n$ is small. Compose $T_n\to D_n$ with this cocone; the cocartesian precomposition equivalence in [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] makes it an active cocone $\bar T_n$ with apex $c_n$ whose unary push is $\bar D_n$. Tensoring on either side preserves these $K_n$-colimits by hypothesis. The elementary criterion of step 2 therefore makes $\bar T_n$ operadically colimiting in the sense of [def-coef-operadic-correspondence]. Its base is the canonical cone specified in [lem-coef-operadic-free-cocone-criterion], because each active arrow to $[1]$ is unique in the base and the construction retained its coherent transformation. This works also when $K_n$ is empty, with $c_n$ initial. Now apply the conditional assembly assertion of [lem-coef-operadic-free-cocone-criterion]: $u$ is inert-preserving as a map of generalized operads, its zero-fibres are Kan, and $u_{[0]}$ is an equivalence, exactly as required. It produces an $\mathcal N$-algebra $A_B$ and $\eta_B:B\to u^*A_B$ with all active slice cocones operadically colimiting. No choice of independent operations or coherence on the $c_n$ is being assumed; assembly is precisely the conditional theorem used here.

source.place: Proposition A.2.10, Proposition A.4.4 and Theorem A.4.6 Read online; agent reconstruction, archive WANTED.

proof.text: The final assertion of [lem-coef-operadic-free-cocone-criterion] identifies, by the specified map $h\mapsto u^*h\circ\eta_B$, $\operatorname{Map}(A_B,C)$ with $\operatorname{Map}(B,u^*C)$ for every $C$. Apply the opposite assertion of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] to $u^*$, taking its full domain of universal arrows: it assembles these pairs into a coherent functor $u_!^{\mathcal V}$ with unit $\eta$ and the coherent-diagram mapping-space adjunction. Choose the functorial pairs among the operadically free pairs of step 3; any comparison compatible with their universal arrows is an equivalence by the same mapping-space property, so their active colimit property is retained. Thus $A_B=u_!^{\mathcal V}B$ has the required unit-induced adjunction. For $B\in\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal W)$, push its small active slice diagram to $D_n^{\mathcal W}$ by the same cited transport statement, take its ordinary colimit in $\mathcal W$, and use separate tensor preservation in $\mathcal W$ in the context calculation of step 2. Conditional assembly and its mapping-space property then give a universal pair in $\mathcal W$ for every $B$. Applying the dual parametric assertion to these pairs gives the coherent $u_!^{\mathcal W}$ and its unit.

source.place: Proposition A.4.3 and Corollary A.4.5; coherent assembly of universal arrows Read online; agent reconstruction, archive WANTED.

proof.text: Write $A_B=u_!^{\mathcal V}B$, and take its operadically colimiting active cocone at $n$. Apply the empty-context part of the operadic-cocone definition [def-coef-operadic-correspondence] and the unary criterion of step 2: its coherent unary push is an ordinary colimit cocone. The mapping-space comparisons in that criterion are those of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] and [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Strong monoidality, in [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], says that $F$ preserves the cocartesian edges used for this push; hence the unary push of its image is the image under $F$ of that colimit cocone. This is colimiting because the underlying $F$ preserves all small colimits. Tensor in $\mathcal W$ preserves the same small colimits separately, so the context calculation of step 2, now in $\mathcal W$, makes the image active cocone operadically colimiting. This last application tests arbitrary tuples in $\mathcal W$, not only tuples in the image of $F$. Its underlying diagram is exactly the active diagram for $F_{*,\mathcal M}B$, and its cone is induced by $F_{*,\mathcal M}\eta_B$, since postcomposition and restriction commute. The mapping-space assertion of [lem-coef-operadic-free-cocone-criterion] consequently makes $(F_{*,\mathcal N}A_B,F_{*,\mathcal M}\eta_B)$ a universal arrow from $F_{*,\mathcal M}B$ to $u^*$ in $\mathcal W$.

source.place: Corollary A.2.9 and Lemma A.4.7, expanded using Proposition A.2.10 Read online; agent reconstruction, archive WANTED.

proof.text: Compare the universal arrow of step 5 with the chosen one $(u_!^{\mathcal W}F_{*,\mathcal M}B,\eta^{\mathcal W}_{F_{*,\mathcal M}B})$. The adjunction gives a map $\beta_B:u_!^{\mathcal W}F_{*,\mathcal M}B\to F_{*,\mathcal N}u_!^{\mathcal V}B$ whose adjunct is $F_{*,\mathcal M}\eta_B$ after the canonical identification $F_{*,\mathcal M}u^*\simeq u^*F_{*,\mathcal N}$. In the reverse direction the universal arrow of step 5 gives $\gamma_B$ satisfying $u^*\gamma_B\circ F_{*,\mathcal M}\eta_B\simeq\eta^{\mathcal W}_{F_{*,\mathcal M}B}$. The two composites have the same adjuncts as the respective identities. The mapping-space equivalences of [lem-coef-operadic-free-cocone-criterion] therefore supply homotopies $\gamma_B\beta_B\simeq\mathrm{id}$ and $\beta_B\gamma_B\simeq\mathrm{id}$. To retain naturality and higher homotopies, apply the dual coherent-diagram formula of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] to $u^*:\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal N}(\mathcal W)\to\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal W)$, with diagram shape $K=\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal V)$ (its universe clause permits enlarging the ambient universe), taking as its two coherent diagrams $F_{*,\mathcal M}:K\to\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal W)$ and $F_{*,\mathcal N}u_!^{\mathcal V}:K\to\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal N}(\mathcal W)$. It takes the coherent transformation $F_{*,\mathcal M}\eta:F_{*,\mathcal M}\to F_{*,\mathcal M}u^*u_!^{\mathcal V}=u^*F_{*,\mathcal N}u_!^{\mathcal V}$ (postcomposition and restriction commute) to a coherent transformation $\beta:u_!^{\mathcal W}F_{*,\mathcal M}\to F_{*,\mathcal N}u_!^{\mathcal V}$; by its compatibility with evaluation at vertices, its component at $B$ is the $\beta_B$ above, so its defining adjunct is exactly the displayed composite in the statement. Each $\beta_B$ is an equivalence by the pointwise argument just given. By the criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] that a coherent transformation is an equivalence in the functor category if and only if all its vertex components are equivalences (applied in the enlarged universe, in which $K$ is small), $\beta$ is an equivalence of functors, including all higher homotopies. No separately constructed coherent inverse is needed.
